aiReview.summary: Official marketing page for a closed-beta Rust-native terminal workspace with a plugin SDK, TSP surfaces, persistent daemon, and remote/web clients. Directly on-rubric as the core Tern product, but access is waitlisted and implementation quality cannot be verified from the page alone.
evidence: Page title and URL are stencil.so/tern with CLOSED BETA and waitlist CTAs.
Nav includes Plugin SDK (docs.stencil.so/tern) and omp.
Copy covers daemon resume, tern remote serve, tern web serve, TSP frames, tern open --preview, and in-pane blocks.
Discovered from curated awesome-tern README as the official product link.
uncertainty: Cannot verify shipping quality, security of remotes/tokens, or SDK completeness.
Pricing model and open-source status unknown.
Example URLs include a token-looking query string; real auth model is unclear.
aiReview.tagline: Rust-native terminal workspace with persistent remote panes
aiReview.description: Native terminal with a surviving daemon, QUIC remotes, TSP graphics, in-pane files, and block apps. Closed beta via waitlist.
pros: Official site documents daemon persistence, remote serve over QUIC, and multi-client sessions (desktop, iPhone, browser).
Describes Tern Surface Protocol for native drawing of diagrams, math, diffs, and live pages.
Links a Plugin SDK docs site and shows block-style apps (git, SQLite, notebooks, kanban) beside the shell.
Positions a Rust-native workspace as an Electron alternative with zsh/omp examples.
cons: Product is closed beta behind a waitlist; no public binary or source is shown on the page.
Pricing, license, and maintenance signals are not stated.
The excerpt is a marketing demo, not runnable code or API contracts.

aiReview.summary: Official Tern reference for the `tern plugin` CLI: install, link, list, reload, and related verbs that manage the machine plugins folder and session daemon without executing plugin Lua.
evidence: Canonical URL is docs.stencil.so/tern/reference/cli.html with full command synopsis.
Listed in theblazehen/awesome-tern README as Plugin CLI.
States tern plugin never runs plugin Lua and never starts the daemon.
uncertainty: Cannot verify Tern product pricing or CLI binary availability from this page alone.
Cannot verify how often the docs stay in sync with shipped Tern versions.
aiReview.tagline: CLI reference for installing and reloading Tern plugins
aiReview.description: Documents tern plugin subcommands, flags, exit codes, git/local install, and link workflow for the plugins folder.
pros: Covers list, reload, dir, install, remove, link, unlink, and types with flags and examples.
Documents exit codes, JSON output, daemon timeout, and error messages for scripting.
Explains git and local install, --force vs links, and iOS Files-app workaround.
cons: This is a documentation page, not a standalone tool or SDK package.
Install from git requires git on PATH and does not prompt for private-repo credentials.

aiReview.summary: Tern plugin that lenses kubectl into native tables, live Explore, previewed mutations, and GitOps drift; well-documented public beta with tests and MIT license, but small community and macOS-first verification.
evidence: GitHub description and README: Native kubectl views for Tern with sortable tables, Explore, pod shells, previewed changes, GitOps drift.
Topics include tern-plugin, kubernetes, kubectl, gitops, luau.
83 commits, MIT license, screenshots under docs/, tests/ and .github/workflows present.
uncertainty: Cannot verify test coverage quality or CI pass status from the page scrape.
Cannot confirm last-commit recency beyond 83 commits on master.
Linux/remote support remains unverified per README.
aiReview.tagline: Native kubectl tables, Explore, and GitOps drift in Tern
aiReview.description: Lens kubectl into sortable tables, live Explore, pod shells, previewed changes, and GitOps drift reports for the Tern terminal.
pros: Implements a Tern plugin (plugin.toml, plugin/) that claims kubectl/kubecolor get, describe, top, apply, delete, scale, and rollout restart.
README documents sorting, inspectors, Explore keys, mutation previews, secret masking, and GitOps drift plus a CI drift binary.
Repository includes tests, docs, examples, CHANGELOG, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, MIT license, and GitHub workflows.
Install path is tern plugin install github.com/contrafy/tern-kube with Tern 0.6.2+ and kubectl required.
cons: Public beta in active development; v1.0 features are still listed as upcoming.
Only 5 stars and 0 forks; Linux and remote Tern hosts are not verified.
Shell guard is opt-in and bypassable by command kubectl and scripts.

aiReview.summary: Tern Luau plugin that renders jj status/st as themed native cards; macOS-only, display-only, with mise-based dev/smoke tooling and bilingual README.
evidence: README states Luau plugin for Tern that renders jj status/st as native cards.
plugin.toml, host.luau, tests/, and tern-sdk/ present; verified versions listed (Tern 0.4.1, jj 0.45.1).
GitHub shows public repo, 1 star, 1 fork, 7 commits, no About description.
uncertainty: License file not confirmed from the listing.
Cannot verify smoke-test pass rate or live maintenance beyond listed files.
Cannot verify plugin behavior against current Tern beyond documented 0.4.1.
aiReview.tagline: Native Tern cards for Jujutsu status output
aiReview.description: Adds a Tern lens that captures jj status/st and colors change, commit, and file lines as themed cards without replacing Git UI.
pros: Documents a display-only lens for jj status/st with explicit non-goals (no jj ops, no Git UI replacement).
Includes mise tasks for typecheck, isolated dev, smoke tests, and production install vs link.
README covers requirements, command capture limits, and isolation of the development Tern profile.
cons: Requires macOS, a Tern account, and Tern installed at a fixed app path by default.
Repository has no GitHub description, 1 star, 7 commits, and limited community signal.
Only status/st without extra args are captured; log, diff, and other commands stay raw.

aiReview.summary: Tern plugin that lenses jj diff/show git-style unified diffs into a native file list with badges and collapsible hunks. Small MIT repo (one commit, 1 star); requires --git output and is trusted plugin code.
evidence: GitHub description and README: jj diff plugin for Tern.
Install via tern plugin install github.com/zsxawerdu/tern-jj-diff.
Repo files: host.luau, plugin.toml, README, LICENSE, MEMORY.md.
uncertainty: Runtime quality of host.luau not independently executed.
Compatibility with current Tern/jj versions not verified.
Author activity beyond this snapshot unknown.
aiReview.tagline: Native Tern lens for Jujutsu git-style diffs
aiReview.description: Renders jj diff and jj show as collapsible per-file views with status markers, rename sources, and binary notes.
pros: Direct Tern plugin for jj diff/show, filling a documented gap vs built-in jj st/log views.
README covers install, --git requirement, command claims, and output limits.
MIT license and explicit warning that plugins run as trusted code.
cons: Single commit, 1 star, 0 forks; maintenance and community signals are weak.
Lens only works on unified git-style output, not other jj formatters.
Caps at 200 files and 2000 lines per file; later files start collapsed.
